The developer will also ensure the visual aesthetics and interactive elements are polished, ensuring a smooth user journey for both service providers and customers.
Responsibilities:
• Review and improve the overall UI/UX of the website.
• Optimize and refine all pages for mobile and desktop responsiveness.
• Fix inconsistencies in design elements such as fonts, colors, padding, and margins across different devices.
• Ensure all interactive components such as buttons, sliders, forms, and animations function smoothly on both desktop and mobile.
• Polish the front-end design to enhance user engagement and make the site visually appealing.
• Work closely with the back-end developer to ensure front-end elements are properly integrated and aligned with the backend functionality.
• Test across multiple browsers and devices to ensure full compatibility and responsiveness.
Required Skills:
• Strong experience with WordPress themes (preferably Woodmart) and custom CSS.
• Expertise in HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and responsive design.
• Proficiency with mobile-first design principles.
• Experience with Elementor or other page builders for WordPress.
• Ability to fix and polish both design and functionality issues.
• Familiarity with UX/UI best practices for enhancing user interaction and conversion.
Preferred Skills:
• Experience with marketplaces or booking platforms.
• Knowledge of mobile and desktop optimization techniques.
• Familiarity with WordPress performance optimization for faster load times.

Prit Zalavadiya

data.text: Website developement

**Project Overview:**The goal is to develop a website with a structure similar to [MindJournals](https://mindjournals.com/). It will be a website for: growin.to. We already have a backend developed based on Shopify and we want to base on that. The site should be user-friendly, aesthetically clean, mobile-responsive, and optimized for e-commerce. It will serve a dual purpose: blog content and e-commerce, selling digital products.---### Key Features & Pages:1. **Home Page:**   - **Header** with logo, navigation menu (Home, About, Shop, Blog, Contact), and a call-to-action button (e.g., "Shop Now").   - **Hero Section** with a visually engaging banner, featuring a short tagline and a prominent call-to-action button.   - **Featured Products/Collections**: Showcase key product collections.   - **Testimonial Slider**: Showcase customer reviews.   - **Blog Highlights**: Preview of the latest blog posts.   - **Footer**: Include social media links, newsletter sign-up, and legal links (Privacy Policy, Terms).2. **Shop Page:**   - Grid-style product listing with filters (category, price range, popularity, etc.).   - Each product should have a thumbnail, price, short description, and a "Buy Now" button.   - Product detail pages should include image gallery, description, price, reviews, related products.3. **Blog Page:**   - List of blog posts displayed in a grid format with images, title, and short descriptions.   - Each post should include related articles at the bottom.4. **About Page:**   - Informational content about the brand, mission, and values.   - Include a section for team members or founder stories with images and descriptions.---### Functionality & Features:- **Responsive Design**: Mobile, tablet, and desktop compatibility.- **E-commerce Integration**: Full functionality to add products to cart, checkout, and payment gateway integration (Stripe, PayPal, etc.).- **CMS (Content Management System)**: Use existing Shopify- **SEO Optimization**: Proper meta tags, alt texts, and structure to be SEO-friendly.- **Newsletter Integration**: Popup or embedded form to capture emails.- **Social Media Integration**: Links to all major social media platforms.- **Loading Speed**: Optimize for fast loading times.---### Technology Stack:Based on what is on growin.to---### Design Considerations:We will deliver product photos as well as an idea for the design### Deliverables:- Full website files, database export, and installation instructions.- Documentation for future updates and maintenance.- Design assets and source files.Attached is the graphic design we want to go of.

We are seeking an experienced Shopify developer to create a new e-commerce website that replicates and enhances the features of our existing site. The primary goal is to build a user-friendly, visually appealing online store that provides a seamless shopping experience for our customers.Key Responsibilities:1. Website Replication:   - Analyze our current website to understand its features and functionalities.   - Develop a Shopify site that mirrors our existing layout while implementing improvements.2. Feature Enhancement:   - Propose and integrate new features that enhance user experience, such as:     - Improved navigation and search capabilities.     - Enhanced product display options (e.g., zoom, 360-degree views).     - User reviews and ratings system.     - Wishlist and comparison features.3. Global Payment Integrations:   - Implement global payment gateways that support multiple currencies, with a particular focus on Naira payments.   - Ensure smooth and secure transaction processes for international customers.4. Ad Integrations:   - Integrate advertising features to promote products effectively. This includes:     - Social media ad integrations (Facebook, Instagram, etc.).     - Google Ads setup and management.     - Retargeting ads for previous site visitors.5. Mobile Optimization:   - Ensure the website is fully responsive and optimized for mobile devices, providing a consistent experience across all platforms.6. SEO Best Practices:   - Implement SEO best practices during development to improve organic search visibility.7. Testing & Launch:   - Conduct thorough testing to ensure all functionalities work correctly before the official launch.   - Provide post-launch support for any issues that may arise.

data.text: I’m looking for assistance with implementing a file upload field in the WooCommerce checkout process. The field should only be displayed and required when the customer selects "Bank Transfer" as the payment method. This uploaded file (payment receipt) needs to be stored in the media library, linked to the order, and visible in the WooCommerce admin panel under the order details.
What’s Been Done So Far:
Field registration with woocommerce_checkout_fields.
field display in the checkout form using woocommerce_after_checkout_billing_form and woocommerce_review_order_before_submit.
javaScript logic to toggle the field’s visibility based on payment method selection.
Enforcing enctype on the checkout form to allow file uploads.
PHP validation to require the file only for "Bank Transfer" and process the upload with wp_handle_upload.

Despite these steps, the file is not being captured correctly on form submission. The field is visible and hidden as expected based on payment method selection, but either an error message appears stating that the file was not uploaded, or the file isn’t appearing in $_FILES during checkout processing.
If you have experience with WooCommerce checkout customizations, particularly with file uploads, I would appreciate your help troubleshooting and resolving this issue.

data.text: Overview:
We are CCS, an organisation specialising in corporate workshops and training. https://calcorporatesolutions.com.au/

We’re seeking skilled WordPress talent to give our current website a fresh, professional redesign using pre-designed Figma layouts. The goal is a fast, visually compelling website that is easy for our team to manage and maintain.
A successful project will launch within 3-4 weeks and provide an SEO-friendly, fully responsive website that meets Google’s Core Web Vitals and page speed standards.
Project Scope
1- Platform: WordPress
2- Builder Preference: Either Elementor or Divi, prioritising page speed
3- Mockups: Hi-Fi mockups in Figma: https://tinyurl.com/3r9h62f7
4- Content: Existing content from the live website; images and additional content will be supplied
5- Features: Parallax effects (for headers and specific sections), responsive mega menu, Salesforce form integration for lead collection
Deliverables:1- Page Development: Build website pages per Figma design, adhering closely to the layout, branding, and styling specified.

Thank you for considering my request.

Best regards,
Bharat Chavda

description:
Windows:


  1. Download the installer: Go to the official Git website (https://git-scm.com/downloads) using your web browser.
  2. Select your download: Click on the "Windows" icon to download the installer for Windows.
  3. Run the installer: Once the download is complete, locate the downloaded file (usually named "Git-X.X.X-XXX.exe," where X.X.X-X is the version number) and double-click on it to start the installation process.
  4. Configure installation options:
  5. Select the components you want to install. The default selections are usually sufficient for most users.
  6. Choose the default text editor for Git (you can keep the default editor or choose your preferred one).
  7. Select the "Use Git from the Windows Command Prompt" option. This will enable you to use Git from the Command Prompt or PowerShell.
  8. Choose "Checkout Windows-style, commit Unix-style line endings" to ensure line endings compatibility across platforms.
  9. Choose the default branch name: Set your preferred default branch name. "master" is commonly used, but you can choose something else if you prefer.
  10. Choose the SSH executable: Unless you have specific requirements, it's generally fine to use the OpenSSH default.
  11. Complete the installation: Click "Install" to begin the installation process. Once it's completed, click "Next" and then "Finish" to exit the installer.
  12. Verify the installation: To check if Git is installed correctly, open a Command Prompt or PowerShell and run the following command:
git --version


macOS:

  • Homebrew (recommended):
  • If you have Homebrew installed on your macOS, open Terminal and run the following command:
brew install git
  • If Homebrew is not installed, you can install it first by following the instructions on the Homebrew website (https://brew.sh).
  • Verify the installation: To check if Git is installed correctly, open Terminal and run:
git --version

Please urgently review the following:

Theme or Custom Coding Conflicts: Identify any errors or conflicts within the custom code that might be causing products to appear as out of stock in the Firmhouse checkout. We need a clear explanation of the root cause.

Corrective Action: Outline any required fixes or code adjustments that need to be implemented to resolve this. Testing should be thorough, ensuring the issue is fully resolved across the entire store.
This is a high-priority issue, and we expect timely feedback on the findings and a concrete solution plan. Please prioritize this fix as it’s directly impacting sales.
Thank you for your attention to this matter.
Please note, that for the short term, we're updated the stock of the subscription product variants to solve it.

data.text: Seeking Elite Shopify Designer for Winter Park Shop - Bring Our Vision to Life!

We’re looking for a Professional Shopify designer to help us elevate our Shopify store, Winter Park Shop. Our site is more than just an online store—it’s a digital extension of our beloved Winter Park community in central Florida. We’ve purchased a high-quality theme, but there’s so much more we can do to make it uniquely ours and infuse it with the charm and elegance that defines Winter Park.About Us:  Winter Park Shop was created to reflect the spirit of Winter Park’s iconic landmarks and offer residents and visitors alike a collection of products that evoke a sense of place and pride. From custom apparel to candles and beyond, our products are all about celebrating Winter Park, and our website should showcase that.Project Overview:  We’re looking for an experienced Shopify designer who can take our existing theme and:- Transform it into a visually stunning site that tells the story of Winter Park and resonates with our target audience.- Integrate a small looped video in the hero section that captures the vibe of Winter Park (we’re looking for creativity here!).- Refine every detail on the website to make it cohesive, polished, and centered around the Winter Park essence.- Optimize layout, fonts, color schemes, and visuals to enhance user experience and drive engagement.- Add final touches and plug-ins that will make the site not only beautiful but also functional and easy to navigate.Reference Material:  To help you get a feel for the Winter Park aesthetic, we’ve put together a Google Drive folder with images and references showcasing the landmarks and symbols that define Winter Park, such as:- WPFL Train Station  - WPFL Scenic Boat Tours  - WPFL Peacock  - Park Avenue  - Rollins College  - The Chain of LakesThese images capture the heart of Winter Park, and we’d love for you to creatively incorporate this essence into the website design, helping to build a sense of community and pride for our visitors. https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1_H2dEKWQjeFp24hUBJu1VOQjr_P4pIys?usp=sharingWhat We’re Looking For:- A top-tier Shopify designer with a proven track record in creating high-quality, visually cohesive websites.- Creativity and understanding of place-based design: We need someone who can capture the feeling of Winter Park and bring it to life through design.- Experience with video integration: Knowledge of integrating and designing looped videos into the hero section and other areas.- Attention to detail and brand alignment: Ability to fine-tune elements and create a seamless, luxury-like shopping experience.Why Work With Us:  This isn’t just another Shopify store. Winter Park Shop is a reflection of a close-knit community, and this project is about more than just selling products. It’s about creating a space that locals are proud to visit, shop, and share with others. If you’re a Shopify designer who thrives on creative challenges and wants to make something truly memorable, this is the project for you.How to Apply:  Please submit your portfolio showcasing previous Shopify sites, particularly any that reflect strong brand storytelling or place-based design. Include a brief note on why you think you’re the right fit for this project and how you would approach making Winter Park Shop unforgettable.

data.text: Expert Shopify Developer for Custom Print-on-Demand Marketplace

I’m looking for an experienced Shopify developer to build a custom print-on-demand website. The site will feature a vast catalog of designs and a range of products, similar in style and functionality to Teefury.com.Key Features:• Dynamic Product Images: Product pages must dynamically generate images based on the design and product selected, as creating static images for each combination isn’t feasible.• Bulk Product Page Creation: Ability to upload product pages in bulk through .csv files to streamline product management.Responsibilities:• Develop a responsive and visually appealing front end that closely mirrors Teefury.com, including design selection, product customization, and a smooth checkout process.• Implement a dynamic image generation tool that allows product images to update in real-time based on design and product choice.• Integrate bulk CSV upload capabilities in the back end, allowing easy creation and management of new product pages.• Ensure that the site is optimized for high performance and scalable to support tens of thousands of product listings.Requirements:• Extensive Shopify Development Experience: Demonstrated track record of building custom Shopify stores.• Expertise in Dynamic Image Generation: Knowledge of image processing tools or Shopify apps/plugins for creating real-time product previews.• CSV Bulk Upload Experience: Skilled in creating or using tools that support large-scale product uploads.• Familiarity with UX/UI best practices for optimizing user flow, especially for customization-based e-commerce.• Strong Communication Skills: Clear and proactive communication for discussing project details, timelines, and updates.

data.text: In this task you have to optimize the DOMs by limiting the content to only the required by bundling and also look over the existing structure and find out what can be done to optimize it.

Improving the performance of the DOM in a Vue application involves several techniques aimed at optimizing reactivity, reducing unnecessary re-renders, and ensuring efficient component updates. Here are some strategies you can use:
### 1. *Use `v-if` and `v-show` Wisely*
- *`v-if`* renders elements conditionally, meaning the component and its children are only rendered when needed. It’s suitable for elements that are rarely shown.
- *`v-show`* simply toggles the visibility of an element with CSS, making it faster than `v-if` for frequently toggled elements because the component remains in the DOM.
### 2. *Optimize Lists with `v-for`*
- Always use a unique `:key` when using `v-for` to help Vue track each item, which avoids unnecessary re-renders.
- Be cautious with large lists as they can cause performance issues; consider pagination or lazy-loading large datasets.
- For very large lists, consider using a virtual scroller, like `vue-virtual-scroll-list`, which only renders visible items.
### 3. *Use Computed Properties Instead of Methods in Templates*
- Computed properties are cached based on their dependencies, whereas methods are executed each time the component renders.
- Use computed properties for values that depend on reactive data and are used multiple times in the template.
### 4. *Debounce or Throttle User Input*

- For real-time user inputs (e.g., search filters), debounce or throttle input events to avoid excessive reactivity updates and DOM manipulations. This can be done with JavaScript utilities like Lodash's `debounce` or `throttle`.
### 5. *Minimize Watchers*
- Avoid using too many watchers, as they can add overhead to your application. Instead, use computed properties where possible.
- Only use watchers for asynchronous or side-effect-based tasks (like API calls) triggered by specific data changes.
### 6. *Lazy-Load Components*
- Use dynamic imports with `defineAsyncComponent` to load components only when they’re needed, reducing initial bundle size and load time.
- This is particularly useful for route-based code-splitting.
### 7. *Use Vue's `keep-alive` for Cached Components*

- Wrap components inside `<keep-alive>` when navigating between routes or dynamically switching views. This prevents components from being destroyed and re-rendered, allowing them to retain their state.
### 8. *Limit Reactive Data and Use Non-Reactive Data Where Possible*

- Vue’s reactivity system tracks all reactive properties, which can add overhead. For static or rarely updated data, consider making it non-reactive (using `Object.freeze` or keeping it out of `data` or `state`).
### 9. *Profile and Analyze with Vue Devtools*
- Use Vue Devtools to check which components re-render frequently. This can help identify performance bottlenecks, especially if some components are updating unnecessarily.
### 10. *Avoid Inline Handlers and Bindings in Templates*

- Each time a component re-renders, inline event handlers (like `@click="myFunction()"`) and bindings (like `:class="someClass"`) are re-evaluated, leading to potential performance hits. Move handlers and bindings to methods or computed properties where feasible.
### 11. *Optimize CSS and Reduce DOM Depth*
- Keep the DOMstructure as shallow as possible to reduce rendering complexity.
- Minimize or scope CSS rules to avoid affecting unrelated parts of the DOM and improving repaint performance.
### 12. *Optimize Vue’s Reactive Dependency Tracking*
- For complex reactive data, use libraries like Vue's `reactive` and `ref` only when necessary, as they are part of Vue’s reactive system and can add overhead.
- Use shallow reactive wrappers like `shallowRef` and `shallowReactive` when deep reactivity isn't required.
By following these optimizations, you can significantly improve Vue’s DOM performance and ensure a smoother, more responsive application.
